You are re-reviewing the fix wave after a final whole-branch review. Verdict each finding and inspect the fix diff — nothing else.

Worktree: /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864. W = /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-27-sma-864-no-tool-calls-after-length

## Findings under verification
I1. A cancelled sub-agent via `agent_as_tool` (crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent_as_tool.rs) gave the parent `ToolOutput("")`, which reads as success and can be saved to the session. Required: when `ctx.cancel().is_cancelled()` and the sub-agent's events have no terminal event, return a `ToolError`. Docs: one sentence in core CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` and one in the "The event stream" section of docs/book/src/concepts/agent-loop.md: a cancelled run can end its stream with no terminal event; TokioRunner reports `RunError::Cancelled`; a direct `collect` of `Agent::run` gives `Ok`.
I2. crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/driver.rs Temporal test must bind `message` of `ErrorKindPayload::Other` and assert substrings from the real `ToolCallsNotRun` Display text.
I3. Core and runtime-temporal CHANGELOGs must say: if the tool call arguments are not complete JSON, or the stream has no `Finish`, the `call_model` activity fails with the reassembly text (verify against crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/activities.rs ~110).
M1. Core upgrade note names an OpenAI-compatible server that sends no `finish_reason` as one example.
M2. agent.rs: the `is_cancelled()` check comes before the `chat_span`/`run_span` "ERROR" records.
M3. tool_calls_not_run.rs `cut_call_is_not_recorded_in_the_session` has a positive assert that the log is not empty.
M4. model.rs `finish()` calls `self.tool_call_names()` instead of copying it; the long doc line is wrapped.

## The fix
Report: W/final-fix-report.md
Fix base: 73666f03  Head: e2b20ca6
Diff file: W/review-73666f03..e2b20ca6.diff

Check in particular, for I1: (a) the check cannot turn a sub-agent that completed normally (a terminal event present) and was cancelled afterwards into an error; (b) the new test proves the error path (RED evidence in the report); (c) the chosen error `ToolError::Other("sub-agent run was cancelled")` is reasonable given ToolError has no cancel variant. For M2: the cancel path still yields no terminal event and the non-cancel path still records ERROR. Prose: ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English (≤25 words per descriptive sentence, active voice).

Read-only: never run git checkout, switch, reset, rebase, stash, restore, commit, or anything that changes HEAD or the index. Do not dispatch subagents. You may run one focused test if a doubt needs it.

content.text:
### Findings

- **I1: ADDRESSED.**
  - Code: `agent_as_tool.rs:197` returns `ToolError::Other("sub-agent run was cancelled")` when `ctx.cancel().is_cancelled()` and `!result.events.iter().any(|e| e.is_terminal())`.
    - (a) A run that completed normally has `RunCompleted` (or another terminal event). `is_terminal` at `agent.rs:572` covers Completed, Failed, Deferred and Stopped. So a normal run cancelled afterwards still returns `Ok`.
    - (b) The test `agent_as_tool_cancelled_sub_run_is_a_tool_error` makes a model that cancels the run and emits a tool-call delta with no `Finish`. The report records RED as a panic with `ToolOutput { content: String("") }`, then GREEN after the fix. I did not re-run it.
    - (c) `Other` is reasonable because the report says `ToolError` has only `InvalidArgs`, `Denied` and `Other`. I did not open the enum. The message contains "cancelled", which the test asserts.
  - Docs: the core CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` has the sentence. `agent-loop.md` carries all three facts: no terminal event, `TokioRunner` gives `RunError::Cancelled`, and a direct `collect` gives `Ok`.
  - Wording gap: the CHANGELOG sentence says `AgentAsTool` now returns a `ToolError`, but it does not mention `TokioRunner` or `collect`. You asked for one sentence in each file, so this is acceptable.
- **I2: ADDRESSED.** `driver.rs` now binds `message` from `ErrorKindPayload::Other` and asserts it contains "not run" and "Length". Both substrings come from the real Display text: `tool_calls_not_run_text` in `agent.rs:1877` gives "…ended with Length, so the tool calls were not run: …".
- **I3: ADDRESSED.** Both CHANGELOGs state the rule. This matches `activities.rs:~110`: `acc.finish().map_err(|message| ErrorKindPayload::Other { message })`. The `call_model` activity fails with the reassembly text.
- **M1: ADDRESSED.** The core upgrade note names an OpenAI-compatible server that sends no `finish_reason`.
- **M2: ADDRESSED.**
  - The `is_cancelled()` return now comes before both `chat_span.record("otel.status_code", "ERROR")` and `run_span.record(...)`.
  - The cancel path still returns with no terminal event.
  - The non-cancel path still records ERROR, because the two records follow the cancel check unconditionally.
- **M3: ADDRESSED.** `cut_call_is_not_recorded_in_the_session` now asserts that the log holds a `UserMessage`. This guards against a vacuous pass.
- **M4: ADDRESSED.** `finish()` calls `self.tool_call_names()`, and the doc comment is wrapped.

### New issues in the fix diff

- **Critical:** none.
- **Important:** none.
- **Minor:**
  - The `is_cancelled()` check now runs after the model stream, so a cancel that arrives between the stream end and the check is still treated as cancelled. That is the same behaviour as before.
  - The test model calls `self.0.cancel()` inside `invoke`, so the token is already cancelled when the stream starts. That is enough to test the path.

### Out-of-Scope Observations

- `ToolError` has no cancel variant. A dedicated one would be cleaner, but it is a public API change and out of scope here.
- A sub-agent that is cancelled and also failed is outside the new check. Its `RunFailed` is a terminal event, so it takes the normal path.
- The CHANGELOG sentences are in simple English. The long first upgrade-note bullet is still near 40 words across its two sentences, and each sentence is under 25.

### Verdict: All addressed, no new Critical/Important

- M4: ADDRESSED. finish() calls self.tool_call_names(); the doc line is wrapped.

### New issues in the fix diff
- Critical: none.
- Important: none.

### Out-of-Scope Observations
- ToolError has no cancel variant. Adding one is a public API change, so out of scope.
- A sub-agent that is cancelled and also failed has RunFailed, which is a terminal event, so it takes the normal path and the new check does not apply.
- The CHANGELOG sentences are simple English. The first upgrade-note bullet is long (about 40 words over two sentences), and each sentence is under 25 words.

### Verdict: All addressed, no new Critical/Important
